title: Ivo and the Static
premise: Elodie Yarrow smuggles memories between the two halves of humanity — the orbital Belt and the cryo-ark fleet that fled Earth's collapse — until a manifest lists a passenger aboard the Meridian, an ark that never launched. The name belongs to Ivo, a man whose recorded memories Elodie has carried for years without knowing they were contraband from a future that hasn't happened. Following the static-laced signal to the Meridian's drydock, she discovers the arks can only wake one half of humanity: the sleepers or the survivors, and Ivo is the archive holding the choice. In the end, Elodie refuses both options, broadcasting Ivo's memories to every ship so each person must choose their own half — and she stays awake with him in the dark between worlds.
about_author: Ivo Ishikawa spent nine years as a freight dispatcher on the Osaka–Lagrange run before turning to fiction, and his prose still carries the clipped rhythm of traffic control. He writes about people who live in the gaps between official records.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Blood
chapters.summary: Elodie runs a memory shipment through Belt customs, hiding stolen recollections inside her own neural signature. POV: Elodie. The beat is competence and loneliness — she's the best at what she does because she has nothing waiting for her at either end.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Was
chapters.summary: A customs broker offers Elodie double pay to verify a passenger list for the Meridian, an ark officially scrapped decades ago. Her own alias appears on it. POV: Elodie. The emotional beat is vertigo — her carefully anonymous life suddenly has a paper trail she never wrote.

chapters.title: Static on the Long Route
chapters.summary: Elodie traces the signal to a decommissioned relay station and finds recordings of Ivo's memories — childhood on Earth, the launch that never happened — mixed with her own smuggled cargo. POV: Elodie. The beat is haunted recognition; someone has been curating her life.

chapters.title: The Man in the Drydock
chapters.summary: At the Meridian's hidden berth, Elodie meets Ivo: not a ghost but an archivist grown from the ship's memory banks, who believes he lived the lives he stores. POV: Ivo. The beat is fragile wonder — he knows her better than anyone alive, and he may be no one at all.

chapters.title: Two Halves of One Choice
chapters.summary: Ivo reveals the ark council's secret: power reserves allow waking either the five million sleepers or the ten million Belt-born survivors, never both. His archive holds the deciding algorithm. POV: alternating. The beat is dread — Elodie realizes why her name was planted on the manifest.

chapters.title: What the Council Paid For
chapters.summary: Ark security arrives to seize Ivo; Elodie learns the broker who hired her works for the faction that wants the sleepers culled. She escapes with Ivo into the ship's dead decks. POV: Elodie. The beat is betrayal hardening into resolve — she was always meant to be disposable.

chapters.title: Memories We Stole Together
chapters.summary: Hiding among frozen colonists, Elodie and Ivo share his archived memories directly, falling into a love built from borrowed pasts neither fully trusts. POV: Ivo. The beat is tenderness shadowed by doubt — if he's only storage, what exactly is she falling for?

chapters.title: The Waking Vote
chapters.summary: Cornered in the cryo-bay, Ivo is forced to run the algorithm while the council watches; it returns a verdict neither side expected: insufficient data, because it cannot weigh love against duty. POV: alternating. The beat is the climax's pivot — the machine confesses its own limits.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Elodie jacks Ivo into the fleet-wide relay and transmits every archived memory to all thirteen ships, giving every waking mind the full weight of both halves' lives. The council's authority dissolves into a species-wide argument. POV: Elodie. The beat is defiant hope at maximum cost — she burns her smuggling network to do it.

chapters.title: Awake in the Dark Between
chapters.summary: Months later, ships wake in staggered shifts chosen by their own crews, and the first messages travel between reconciled halves of humanity. Elodie remains aboard the Meridian with Ivo, who is learning to make new memories instead of storing old ones. POV: alternating. The beat is quiet resolution — survival was never the price; forgetting was.
